entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pham Ngu Lao was a prominent general of the Trần dynasty during the reigns of three successive emperors: Nhân Tông, Anh Tông, and Minh Tông. His talent was noticed by Prince Hưng Đạo Trần Quốc Tuấn who married his adopted daughter to Pham Ngu Lao and recommended him for the royal court.

Pham Ngũ Lão was renowned as a skilled commander in battlefield, one of the few commanders of the Vietnamese army during the second and third Mongol invasion who did not come from the Trần clan. He played a crucial role in defending Vietnam against the Mongols, utilizing innovative tactics that allowed him to repel multiple invasions.

Pham Ngũ Lão's military prowess and strategic brilliance earned him recognition as a leader among his peers, with many historians crediting him with helping to secure Vietnam's independence during this tumultuous period. His legacy continues to be studied by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the complexities of medieval Vietnamese history and the evolution of its military strategies.

The exact date of Pham Ngũ Lão's birth is unknown, but his death in 1320 solidified his place as one of Vietnam's most revered historical figures. His impact on Vietnamese society extends beyond his military accomplishments, with many regarding him as a symbol of national pride and resilience.
